headline: CSIRO runs sunlight-driven direct air capture field trial at its WA In-Situ Laboratory, timed for GHGT-18
summary: CSIRO is demonstrating Seattle start-up Banyu Carbon's photoacid, sunlight-driven DAC unit at its In-Situ Laboratory in WA's south-west — reportedly the first carbon-capture technology deployed at the site — with the month-long trial timed to run for GHGT-18 delegates; CO2 is vented rather than stored during the test.
co2crc_note: A novel DAC technology field-trialled on Australian soil at CSIRO's ISL during GHGT-18 (co-hosted by CO2CRC) — directly relevant to CO2CRC's capture-technology and field-testing agenda.
extractor_note: R&D field demo; no money figure. 'Industry first' is the trade outlet's framing (first capture tech at the ISL site). Article body not fetchable this run (egress block); summary built from verified alerts-floor date + prior CSIRO 20 Oct pre-announcement.

headline: GHGT-18 opens in Perth with 1,000+ delegates — CO2CRC among the co-hosts
summary: The 18th Greenhouse Gas Control Technologies Conference, the sector's flagship global scientific meeting run by the IEA Greenhouse Gas R&D Programme, opened at Crown Perth (25-29 Oct) — the first time it has been held in Western Australia — co-hosted by CSIRO, CO2CRC, Geoscience Australia and Australian Energy Producers.
co2crc_note: CO2CRC is a co-host of GHGT-18 — the sector's flagship global conference, held in CO2CRC's home country for the first time in WA; a marquee week for Australian CCS visibility.
extractor_note: Sector-event notice, no financial dimension. Included for CO2CRC home-country relevance; low hard-news value.

headline: Trade press questions whether Commonwealth's A$3m grant to Pilot Energy's Mid West CCS scheme will be recovered
summary: Energy News Bulletin examined public exposure on the ~A$3m initial Commonwealth grant (part of a ~A$6.5m CCUS Development Fund package) backing Pilot Energy's Cliff Head CO2-storage conversion and Capture6 DAC demonstration, against the small-cap developer's funding and delivery challenges.
